questions.prompt: Why use the csv module instead of splitting each line on commas?
choices: A quoted field can contain a comma, and split would break the row there
split does not work on files
questions.explain: "Lovelace, Ada" is one field with a comma in it. csv knows about the quotes; split sees three fields where there are two.

questions.prompt: What does csv.DictReader use the first line of the file for?
choices: As the column names for every row after it
As the first row of data
questions.explain: The header becomes the keys, which is why row["score"] works without you saying which position that is.

questions.prompt: What type is row["score"] straight out of a CSV file?
questions.explain: A file is text, so everything read out of one is text until you convert it. That is the source of more early bugs than anything else in this course.

questions.prompt: What does the with statement guarantee when reading a file?
choices: The file is closed when the block ends, even if an error happens
questions.explain: Leaving the block, for any reason, closes the file. That is the whole job of with.

questions.prompt: Match each idea to its meaning.
right: Can contain a comma without creating another column
Converts a numeric field from text before arithmetic
questions.explain: CSV header: Supplies field names for DictReader. Quoted field: Can contain a comma without creating another column. int(row["score"]): Converts a numeric field from text before arithmetic.

questions.prompt: Arrange these steps in the intended order.
items: Open the CSV file as text
Create a DictReader from the file
Read rows and convert the score values
questions.explain: Read with a CSV parser before converting fields; conversion precedes arithmetic.

questions.label: Predict the first line of output (without surrounding quotes).
questions.prompt:
import csv
from io import StringIO

text = 'name,score\n"Lee, Jo",8\nAda,10\n'
rows = list(csv.DictReader(StringIO(text)))
print(rows[0]["name"])
print(sum(int(row["score"]) for row in rows))

First output line: ___
questions.explain: The comma inside the quoted name belongs to that one field. DictReader keeps Lee, Jo together. The score values start as "8" and "10", then int converts them before summing. StringIO lets this small example behave like a text file without requiring an upload.
